werkzeug.k1-zaehlen.name: Counting
werkzeug.k1-zaehlen.regel: Rule: Chapter 1, “Counting the values of attackers and defenders”. The app counts every piece that attacks or defends the square, including pieces in a battery (such as a queen behind your own pawn). For the balance, each side captures with its cheapest piece first and stops as soon as further captures would cost material.
werkzeug.k1-zaehlen.erklaerung: Tap a square on the board. The app counts who attacks it and who defends it, shows both with arrows as in the book, and tells you whether capturing wins material. Tap the same square again to see the book's markings once more.
werkzeug.k1-zaehlen.legende: Red arrows: the attackers of the square. Gold arrows: its defenders. Red: the square being counted.
werkzeug.k1-angriffsregel.name: Attack rule
werkzeug.k1-angriffsregel.regel: Rule: Chapter 1, the golden attack rule. The attack sector is the files of the wing where the enemy king stands (e to h, a to d, in the middle c to f), in his half of the board. Attackers: every piece of yours except king and pawns that attacks a square of the sector; bishop, rook and queen also through one of your own pieces that can move away (like the queen on d1 behind the knight on f3 in Fig. 1.37). Defenders: enemy pieces except king and pawns that stand in the sector; pinned and overloaded ones don't count. Rule of thumb: at least three attackers and more attackers than defenders. Still, don't count purely mechanically: a king without an escape square can fall to a single piece.
werkzeug.k1-angriffsregel.erklaerung: The app counts your attackers and the defenders in the sector around the enemy king. Below it shows the same for your opponent's attack on your king.
werkzeug.k1-angriffsregel.legende: Gold: the attackers. Red: the defenders. Gray: the border of the sector around the king.
werkzeug.k1-todsuenden.name: Deadly sins
werkzeug.k1-todsuenden.regel: Rule: Chapter 1, the four deadly sins of the opening phase, checked along the moves in the move bar as long as one side has not yet reached its three opening goals. Early queen: the queen leaves her starting square while at least two of your minor pieces are still on their starting squares. Greed for material: a capture that is not a recapture while your own king has not yet castled and at least two minor pieces are still at home. Passivity: a move with the a- or h-pawn that captures nothing and attacks no piece afterwards, while at least three of your minor pieces are still at home. King in the center: not yet castled after move ten. For each side and each sin, the app names the first finding (automatic assessment). These are only candidates: whether the move really does harm is for you to check, because sometimes bringing the queen out early, for example, makes sense.
werkzeug.k1-todsuenden.erklaerung: The app goes through the moves up to the position shown and looks for candidates for the four deadly sins from Chapter 1: early queen, greed for material, passivity and king in the center. Whether a candidate really is a sin is for you to decide.
werkzeug.k1-todsuenden.legende: Red: the piece involved in a possible deadly sin.
werkzeug.k1-roentgen.name: X-ray
werkzeug.k1-roentgen.regel: Rule: Chapter 1, Chess X-ray rule. The app looks for all checks, captures and threats of both sides. For the opponent it asks what he would have if he were to move again right now. Every capture is shown with its exchange balance (each side captures with the cheapest piece first). A move threatens something if it would win material or give mate on the next move. Question 4, “Optimization”, can only be answered by the engine, so the app refers you to the “Engine” button for it.
werkzeug.k1-roentgen.erklaerung: The four questions of the Chess X-ray rule at a glance: which checks, which captures and which threats do both sides have? For question 4, the best quiet move, use the “Engine” icon next to the board.
werkzeug.k1-roentgen.legende: Gold arrows: checks, winning captures and threats of the side in view. Red arrows: the opponent's checks and threats. Gray arrows: captures that win nothing (exchange).
werkzeug.k2-eroeffnung.name: Opening
werkzeug.k2-eroeffnung.regel: Rule: Chapters 2 and 3. The app knows every position from the move sequences of the openings (Chapter 2) and gambits (Chapter 3), including all branches. It compares the placement of the pieces, the side to move and the castling rights, not the move order: the app recognizes the opening even after a transposition. If the position belongs to several openings (such as after 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6), the opening is still open.
werkzeug.k2-eroeffnung.erklaerung: The app looks up the position shown in the book's openings and gambits and names the opening, the variation and its profile. The button takes you to the place in the book.
werkzeug.k2-zielbilanz.name: Goal balance
werkzeug.k2-zielbilanz.regel: Rule: Chapter 2, the three checks of the goal balance. Center: is one of your pawns on d4, e4, d5 or e5? Then yes. If the opponent, with the move, could capture it on its square at a profit according to the exchange calculation, it counts as “attacked”, and the engine checks with a short thinking time whether the capture still wins at least one pawn after the best reply; only if all center pawns are then hanging is the center “partly”. Without center pawns, control by pieces counts: if your pieces attack at least two of the four center squares directly (without a battery behind them) at least as often as the opponent, yes; with one square, partly (automatic assessment). Development: have all four minor pieces left their starting squares? Traded ones count as done; two or three done: partly, at most one: no. King safety: has the king castled (it stands on the back rank on a, b, c, g or h), and are at least two of the three pawns in front of it at most one square away from their starting squares? Castled with a loosened shield: partly. If the king stands on a, b, c, g or h one rank in front of the back rank (such as h7 after Kxh7), it had castled and was then moved or chased: partly. Not castled: no.
werkzeug.k2-zielbilanz.erklaerung: The app draws up the goal balance from Chapter 2 for the position shown: center, development and king safety for both sides, each with yes, partly or no. The board shows the side in view.
werkzeug.k2-zielbilanz.legende: For the side in view. Gold: developed minor pieces, center pawns or controlled center squares, shield pawns. Red: minor pieces on their starting squares. King gold, gray or red according to the king safety goal. Gray: attacked center pawns (the engine checks whether they are hanging) and the remaining center squares.
werkzeug.k4-falle.name: Trap?
werkzeug.k4-falle.regel: Rule: Chapter 4. The offer is the planned move if it captures something (in the figure, the next move in the book), otherwise the capture that wins the most according to the exchange calculation (W5). The engine evaluates the position after this capture and the best other move. If the capture is at least one pawn worse, it is a trap (red), and the best other move is the rescue (gold); otherwise the material is a real gift (automatic assessment). If the figure is one of the book's stop moments, the book's trap check appears below.
werkzeug.k4-falle.erklaerung: The app checks whether the material on offer is a gift or bait: the engine compares the capture with the best other move. At the book's traps you also get the trap check from Chapter 4.
werkzeug.k4-falle.legende: Once the engine is done: red arrow for the capture if it is a trap, gold arrow for the better move. If it is a gift, the capture is gold.
werkzeug.k4-prueffragen.name: Check questions
werkzeug.k4-prueffragen.regel: Rule: Chapter 4, the three check questions. F1 Why question: whenever material is offered, ask why the opponent allows it (prepared text; on offer is the planned capture or a capture that wins according to the exchange calculation). F2 Two replies ahead: calculate at least two of the opponent's replies (the engine shows the strongest). F3 Pin check: all pins, absolute (against the king) or relative (against a more valuable piece), plus hidden ones: there is still another piece between the long-range piece and the pinned piece; if it moves away, the pin against the king is there. With a planned move (in the figure, the next move in the book), the app compares the pins against you before and after the move: if one appears or remains, that is the second pin.
werkzeug.k4-prueffragen.erklaerung: The app asks the three check questions from Chapter 4 before the next move in the book.
werkzeug.k4-prueffragen.legende: Gray: pin lines. Gold: the planned move. Red: pins after the planned move.
werkzeug.k3-faktorenbilanz.name: Factor balance
werkzeug.k3-faktorenbilanz.regel: Rule: Chapter 3, the factor balance. Material: the sum of the rule-of-thumb values from Chapter 1 (pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9) for each side; the scale tips toward the side with more. Time: knights, bishops, queen and rooks that are not on a starting square of their kind count as in play (including the rook after castling); king and pawns don't count, traded pieces count for neither side, pieces that returned home no longer count. If Black is to move, one piece is subtracted from White's lead. King safety (automatic assessment): good without the enemy queen; castled is good, unless your own pawn is missing on a file in front of the king and an enemy rook or the queen stands there (partly; the piece is named when no pawn stands between it and the king: an open file without pawns, a half-open one only with enemy pawns) or the shield is thin and three neighboring squares are attacked (bad); in the middle partly, bad with an open king file and an attacked neighboring square; a king in check is at most partly. Activity (automatic assessment): bad with no piece in play or when the opponent has two threats; good when pieces in play, attacked targets and threats together are at least two more than the opponent's; otherwise partly. Durability according to the table in Chapter 3. Whether the compensation is enough is only judged by the engine. If the side to move is in check, the balance is preceded by the hint to first calculate the check and the tactics to the end; if it is mated or stalemated, the game is decided and there is no balance.
werkzeug.k3-faktorenbilanz.erklaerung: The app draws up the factor balance from Chapter 3 for the position shown: material and time with a scale, king safety and activity for each side, plus how long the advantages last. The board shows the side in view.
werkzeug.k3-faktorenbilanz.legende: For the side in view. Gold: pieces in play and threats (arrows). Gray: pieces still at home and other attacks (arrows). King gold, gray or red according to its safety. Red: attacked squares next to it, enemy rooks and queens on a line to it with no pawns in between.
werkzeug.k4-warnsignale.name: Warning signs
werkzeug.k4-warnsignale.regel: Rule: Chapter 4, the five warning signs, defined precisely in the specification. W1 Undefended piece: every piece except the king that no piece of its own side defends; pawns only if they are attacked. W2 Dangerous line: on the ray of a bishop, rook or queen stands a piece, and directly behind it the other side's king, queen or rook, more valuable than the front piece or undefended (pin, skewer or discovered attack); or the king or queen stands in front and directly behind it an undefended piece of its own side, even a pawn (if the queen moves away, the piece behind falls). W3 King without air: the king has no neighboring square that is empty or occupied by the opponent and not attacked by the opponent. W4 Double duty: without this piece, the opponent could immediately win material or give mate in two places, or it is the only defender against a mate (automatic assessment). A duty also includes a capture that is already possible but only loses because the piece recaptures, if the opponent then wins elsewhere after its recapture. W5 Gift: enemy material that can be captured at a profit according to the exchange calculation; whether it is bait is only judged by the engine. Apparently free: material defended only by relatively pinned pieces; the exchange calculation counts them, because a pinned piece still has an effect (Chapter 7).
werkzeug.k4-warnsignale.erklaerung: The app looks for the five warning signs from Chapter 4 on both sides. If you see a warning sign, calculate especially carefully.
werkzeug.k4-warnsignale.legende: Red with label: warning signs for the side in view, danger here. Gold with label: signs for the opponent, and W5, what he seems to give away.
werkzeug.ziehen.name: Move
werkzeug.ziehen.erklaerung: Play on yourself: tap a piece of the side to move, then its target square (the dots show where it may go). Your moves appear in the move bar. If you hit the book's move, the book continues; “Back to the book line” discards your moves.
werkzeug.engine.name: Engine
werkzeug.engine.erklaerung: The engine (Stockfish) calculates on your device, even without internet. It evaluates the position in pawns: plus means White is better, minus means Black is better. Below are the three best continuations. If the engine ever disagrees with one of the book's move marks, that is not an error: the book evaluates for humans, that is, the idea, the lesson and the practical chances; the engine only the best continuation by calculation. Small differences of a few tenths hardly matter over the board, and in deep endgames and studies the engine sometimes does not see far enough.

eroeffnung.kurz.spanisch: White attacks the defender of e5 with the bishop on b5 and builds up pressure slowly. Lots of theory, rewarding for patient players.
eroeffnung.kurz.italienisch: White develops quickly, castles early and aims at f7 with the bishop on c4. The quiet lines are easy to learn; the lines with c3 and d4 are sharp.
eroeffnung.kurz.schottisch: White opens the center as early as move three, followed by clear piece play. Less theory than in the Spanish Game.
eroeffnung.kurz.russisch: Black does not defend e5 but attacks e4 instead. Solid and often symmetrical; there is one well-known trap you need to know.
eroeffnung.kurz.sizilianisch: Black fights for d4 from the side with c5, and the position becomes unbalanced; often the two sides attack on opposite wings. For players who want to play for a win with Black and like to calculate.
eroeffnung.kurz.damengambit: White offers the c-pawn to lure the d5 pawn away from the center. A strategic fight for the center, shaped by the pawn structures from Chapter 5.
eroeffnung.kurz.london: White almost always plays the same setup with the bishop on f4. Little risk and little theory, leaving more time for tactics and endgames.
eroeffnung.kurz.trompowsky: White puts the bishop on g5 and often gives it up for the knight on f6 to weaken Black's pawns. Active, with a manageable amount of theory.
eroeffnung.kurz.franzoesisch: Black answers with e6 and d5; closed positions with pawn chains arise. For patient planners.
eroeffnung.kurz.carokann: Black supports d5 with c6 and keeps the c8 bishop mobile. Solid and calm, with clear pawn breaks.
eroeffnung.kurz.koenigsindisch: Black first leaves the center to White and attacks on the kingside later. Sharp and theory-heavy; you have to put up with a lack of space.
eroeffnung.kurz.zweispringer: Two Knights: Black attacks e4 at once with Nf6, and the game turns tactical. Bishop's Opening: White plays Bc4 early and stays calm and flexible.
eroeffnung.kurz.nimzoindisch: Black pins the knight on c3 with Bb4 and fights for e4. It is often about the bishop pair against a weakened pawn structure.

ich.wertung.erklaerung: Elo system as in a chess club: wins raise your rating, losses lower it, more so against stronger opponents. Your first rated game sets the rating to the playing strength the app estimates from your accuracy (midpoint of the chess.com and Lichess scales). Every further game counts like a game against a player with the opponent's fixed rating from the opponent selection (since 0.2.85; before that, the estimate from the game; K = 32 in the first ten games, 20 after that). Unlike “Your playing strength” in Play, which only measures the accuracy of your last ten games, results are what count here. Rated games are finished games against the engine from the starting position with the “Rated game” box checked, once the analysis is done; games from figures or set-up positions and games with takebacks do not count. Your first rated game needs ten of your own moves before the decision so the app can estimate your playing strength; after that every game counts, even a short one.

trainer.struktur.name: Structure spotter
trainer.struktur.ablauf: Only the skeleton is visible. You answer the four guiding questions by tapping (holes, weak pawns, direction, good or bad bishop) and choose the matching plan statement.
strukturtrainer.auftrag.felder: Step {nummer} of {gesamt}: Which squares on your 5th and 6th ranks can no enemy pawn attack anymore? Tap these strong squares. If there are none, tap “Check” right away.
strukturtrainer.auftrag.bauern: Step {nummer} of {gesamt}: Tap all the weak pawns of both sides: isolated, doubled or backward. If there are none, tap “Check” right away.
strukturtrainer.keine.felder: There is no square on your 5th and 6th ranks here that no enemy pawn can attack anymore.
strukturtrainer.keine.bauern: There are no isolated, doubled or backward pawns here.
strukturtrainer.stufenText: Level 1 is easy, level 5 is hard: the more pawn features and pieces, the more there is to keep track of.
struktur.plan.vorpostenBesetzen: Put a knight on the outpost: a square that no enemy pawn can attack anymore.
struktur.plan.lochVermeiden: Avoid pawn moves that leave a hole; keep the squares in front of your own pawns defended.
struktur.plan.luftlochSchaffen: Give your king an escape square (luft) with a small pawn move, but not just in case: only once enemy rooks or the queen can reach the back rank.
struktur.plan.doppelbauerAngreifen: Attack the opponent's doubled pawns with pieces: the two pawns cannot defend each other.
struktur.plan.doppelbauerAufloesen: With your own doubled pawns, keep pieces on the board, use the open file and the bishop pair, and avoid a pure pawn endgame.
struktur.plan.isolaniBlockieren: Blockade the isolani: put a piece, ideally a knight, directly in front of it, trade pieces and steer toward the endgame.
struktur.plan.isolaniVorstossen: Play actively with the isolani and avoid trading pieces where possible: every piece on the board increases your attacking chances.
struktur.plan.haengendeAngreifen: Put pressure on the hanging pawns with rooks and attack their defenders until one of them has to advance; the square in front of the pawn left behind then becomes a hole.
struktur.plan.haengendeVorstossen: Keep the hanging pawns together and look for active piece play; only advance one of them with a concrete threat.
struktur.plan.kettenbasisAngreifen: Attack the pawn chain at its base with a pawn break.
struktur.plan.fluegelDerKette: Play on the wing your own pawn chain points to.
struktur.plan.mehrheitVorstossen: Advance the pawn majority to create a passed pawn.
struktur.plan.minderheitsangriff: Minority attack: advance fewer pawns against the opponent's majority and create weaknesses there.
struktur.plan.raumNutzen: Use the space advantage: regroup your pieces behind your own pawns and avoid exchanges.
struktur.plan.stellungOeffnen: Open the position with a pawn break, because your own pieces are more active.
struktur.plan.stellungSchliessen: Keep the position closed, because your own pieces work better there.
struktur.plan.schlechtenLaeuferTauschen: Regroup the bad bishop, which is stuck behind your own pawns on its color, or trade it for a good enemy bishop.
struktur.plan.gutenLaeuferBehalten: Keep the good bishop and put your own pawns on the other color.
struktur.plan.springerStattLaeufer: In a closed position, prefer the knight to the bishop and trade the bishop.

trainer.endspiel.name: Endgame trainer
endspiel.kurz.text: No engine, one question each: square, opposition, key squares and “Which recognition pattern?” (Chapters 8 and 9).
drill.quadrat.frage: Does the black king catch the pawn? Count the square (careful: who is to move?).
drill.quadrat.regel: Rule: Chapter 8, the rule of the square. If the king can step into the pawn's square, it catches the pawn; if the pawn's side is to move, the square counts after its move. Gold: the square being measured.
drill.opposition.regel: Rule: Chapter 8, the opposition. If the kings stand on a file, rank or diagonal with an odd number of squares between them, the side that is not to move has the opposition. Otherwise neither has it.
drill.schluesselfelder.frage: Which square is a key square of the white pawn? If the white king reaches it, White wins.
drill.schluesselfelder.regel: Rule: Chapter 8, table of key squares (2nd to 4th rank: three squares two ranks in front of the pawn; 5th and 6th rank: six squares; rook pawn: the neighboring file at the very front). Gold: all key squares.
drill.bild.regel: Rule: Chapter 9, review: the recognition patterns. Plan in brief: {plan}
endspiel.stufenText: Level 1 is easy (mate with the queen), level 5 is hard (rook endgames where only one move works). Rated by topic and by whether the first move is the only one.
endspiel.ablaufText: You play the position out against the engine at full strength. Goal: win (mate or promotion) or hold the draw for twelve moves. If the position tips over, the app shows the move that would have held it.
endspiel.ziel.gewinn: {farbe}: win this position against the engine.
endspiel.ziel.remis: {farbe}: hold the draw against the engine.
endspiel.hilfeZug: The golden arrow is the engine's move for you.
endspiel.hilfeRechnet: The engine is still calculating, the hint is coming.
endspiel.erreicht.umwandlung: Promoted, and the position is won. Goal reached.
endspiel.erreicht.gehalten: Held for twelve moves, the engine cannot break through. Goal reached.
endspiel.verfehlt.gekippt: {ziel} is gone: according to the engine, the position has tipped over.
endspiel.merksatz.damenmatt: Queen and king work together: the queen locks the enemy king in an ever smaller box, your own king comes closer, and only then comes mate. Before every queen move, check that the enemy king still has a square, or you risk stalemate.
endspiel.merksatz.turmmatt: The rook blocks a rank or file, and your king takes away the squares in front of it from the enemy king. With a waiting move you force it to the edge step by step. Avoid stalemate.
endspiel.merksatz.laeuferpaar: Side by side, the two bishops form a wall the enemy king cannot cross. Your own king pushes it into the corner, and the bishops move the wall along.
endspiel.merksatz.opposition: Opposition: if the kings stand on the same file with one square between them, the side to move has to give way. Take the opposition when you attack, and keep it when you defend. At a greater distance (distant opposition), an odd number of squares in between is what counts.
endspiel.merksatz.schluesselfelder: Key squares: if your king reaches one of the squares two ranks in front of the pawn (from the fifth rank on, also one rank in front of it), the pawn wins, no matter who is to move. The defender keeps the king away from these squares and looks for the opposition.
endspiel.merksatz.quadrat: Rule of the square: imagine a square from the pawn up to the promotion rank. If the king can step into it on its move, it catches the pawn; otherwise the pawn runs through.
endspiel.merksatz.bauernrennen: Pawn race: count the moves both pawns need to promote, and check whether the new queen immediately wins the other one with a check or a skewer.
endspiel.merksatz.durchbruch: Breakthrough: a pawn sacrifice creates a passed pawn the opponent can no longer catch. Calculate all the way to promotion before you sacrifice.
endspiel.merksatz.freibauer: Passed pawns: a distant passed pawn deflects the enemy king, and your king then collects the remaining pawns. With connected passed pawns, the rear one defends the front one; if the king takes the rear one, the front one runs through. Bring your king up first before you advance them.
endspiel.merksatz.zugzwang: Zugzwang: whoever has to move worsens their position with every move. With a waiting move, such as the king's triangle, you hand the move back to the opponent.
endspiel.merksatz.randbauer: Rook pawn: if the defending king reaches the corner in front of the pawn, it is a draw; the attacker cannot get the square next to the promotion square.
endspiel.merksatz.turmendspiel: Rook endgame: the rook belongs behind the passed pawn, the defending king in front of the pawn. Philidor: rook on the sixth rank, then checks from behind. Lucena: the attacker drives the king away and builds the bridge with the rook.
endspiel.merksatz.dameGegenBauer: Queen against pawn on the seventh rank: the queen approaches with checks until the king has to step in front of its pawn; in that pause your king takes one step closer. Against bishop and rook pawns, stalemate lurks.
endspiel.merksatz.leichtfiguren: Minor pieces: opposite-colored bishops often hold the draw if the king blockades the pawns on the other color. The wrong bishop with a rook pawn does not win if the king reaches the corner. A knight stops the pawn if it covers the promotion square in time.
endspiel.stichwort.turmHinterFreibauer: Keyword: rook behind the passed pawn.
endspiel.stichwort.siebteReihe: Keyword: rook on the seventh rank.

App: this app's standard, a middle way; moves in a decided position count half. chess.com: close to chess.com; moves in a decided position hardly count (matches chess.com to within about 6 percentage points on average; chess.com does not publish its formula). werkzeug.k5-vorher.name: Before
werkzeug.k5-vorher.regel: Rule: Chapter 5, the basic law of pawns (“A pawn only defends diagonally forward and can never go back”). The move checked is the planned move (in the figure, the next move in the book) if it is a pawn move, otherwise the last move played. Front: the squares the pawn defends afterwards and did not before. Behind: the squares that no pawn of your own can control any more afterwards (new holes). The four reasons: Squares (a newly controlled square in the center or in the enemy half), Pawn weakness (an enemy pawn no longer passes the protection test afterwards, or one of your own passes it again), Direction (the pawn attacks an enemy pawn afterwards: a lever), Piece (one of your bishops, rooks or your queen reaches more squares afterwards, or the king gets an escape square).
werkzeug.k5-vorher.erklaerung: Step 0 of the skeleton X-ray: before every pawn move, the app asks what it gains in front and gives up forever behind, and which of the four reasons from Chapter 5 it fulfills. Play a pawn move with “Move”, or let the app check the next move in the book.

werkzeug.k5-felder.name: Squares
werkzeug.k5-felder.regel: Rule: Chapter 5, guiding question 1. A hole is a square that no pawn of your own can control any more: on both neighboring files, no pawn of your own stands behind it any more. The app names holes on the opponent's 4th to 6th ranks and marks in red what the opponent can use (one of his pieces reaches the square in one move, or one of his pawns supports it). Gold are the safe squares: enemy holes from your own 4th rank onward, with support from one of your pawns (outposts), and the pieces that can get there. Knight squares are supported and not attacked by any enemy pawn, but can still be attacked as soon as an enemy pawn moves. Kingside (after castling): an advanced shield pawn is a luft hole if its starting square gives the king an escape square (h3: luft on h2), and a hook if an enemy pawn can reach it with a lever; plus holes on the files around the king; without a luft hole and without a rook or queen on the back rank, a back-rank mate threatens.
werkzeug.k5-felder.erklaerung: Guiding question 1 of the skeleton X-ray: which squares can no pawn control any more? The app names your holes that the opponent can use, and the squares where your pieces stand safely. Plus the state of your kingside.
werkzeug.k5-felder.legende: Red: holes the opponent can use. Gold: squares where your own pieces stand safely.
werkzeug.k5-bauern.name: Pawns
werkzeug.k5-bauern.regel: Rule: Chapter 5, guiding question 2, the protection test: can a pawn of your own defend the pawn, now or after it or a neighboring pawn has made a move? If it fails, the app names the reason from the book's table: doubled pawn (D), isolani (I), chain base without support (C), backward (B), hanging pair (H), otherwise U. Plus the number of pawn islands (groups of your own pawns separated by files without a pawn of your own), passed pawns, and the open and half-open files (gray).
werkzeug.k5-bauern.erklaerung: Guiding question 2 of the skeleton X-ray: which pawns can no pawn defend any more? The app names the weak pawns of both sides and the open and half-open files.
werkzeug.k5-bauern.legende: Red with letter: weak pawns (D doubled pawn, I isolani, R backward, H hanging, B chain base without support). Gray: open and half-open files.
werkzeug.k5-richtung.name: Direction
werkzeug.k5-richtung.regel: Rule: Chapter 5, guiding question 3. A chain points from its base to its head; if the head is further to the right (e to h), it points to the kingside, otherwise to the queenside. Space: your pawns in the enemy half and the squares there that they attack. Majority: more of your pawns on one wing (a to d, e to h), with the candidate (no enemy pawn stands in front of it on its file); minority: fewer, but at least one. Lever: a pawn move (also in two moves, such as b2–b4–b5) after which the pawn attacks an enemy pawn. If there is a lever against the base of an enemy chain, it comes first and alone in gold; the others follow in gray as “other levers”. Tension: pawns that could capture each other. The conclusion checks in this order: 1. the direction of the chain; 2. a healthy majority of your own (with a candidate) if no enemy majority has a candidate; 3. an enemy pawn weakness that is fixed or stands on a file that is half-open for you (blockade the square in front of it and attack it with pieces); 4. the minority attack, only with at least two pawns, with a lever and against an enemy majority with a candidate; if your own king stands there, it says “counterplay with pieces” instead; 5. otherwise your own majority.
werkzeug.k5-richtung.erklaerung: Guiding question 3 of the skeleton X-ray: where does the structure point, and where do you have more pawns? The app shows the direction of your chains, your levers and enemy chain bases without support.
werkzeug.k5-richtung.legende: Gray arrows: direction of the chains and other levers. Gold arrows: the lever against the enemy base (if there is none, all levers). Red: enemy chain base without support.
werkzeug.k5-figuren.name: Pieces
werkzeug.k5-figuren.regel: Rule: Chapter 5, guiding question 4. Type of position: open if at most one pawn stands on the d- and e-files (including an isolani, Chapter 6); closed if pawn pairs are locked on both files; mobile with a pawn duo of your own in the center (d4/e4 or d5/e5 with free squares in front); half-open if only one side has pawns on a center file; otherwise mixed. Bad bishop: more of your own fixed pawns on its square color than on the other (fixed: locked, part of a chain, isolated or backward); passive if both diagonals going diagonally forward end at your own pawns. If a bishop that is bad by color stands in front of its own chain (not passive and no fixed pawn of its color further forward than it), it is called “bad by color, but active” and is not red. Knights belong on the safe squares and knight squares from guiding question 1, rooks on open and half-open files. Exchange question: whoever has the weakness keeps pieces; whoever attacks it trades; whoever has more space avoids exchanges.
werkzeug.k5-figuren.erklaerung: Guiding question 4 of the skeleton X-ray: which pieces suit this skeleton, and what do you trade? The app names bad bishops and good squares for your knights.
werkzeug.k5-figuren.legende: Red: a bad bishop. Gold: good squares for the knights, and a bishop that is bad by color but stands actively in front of its own chain.

werkzeug.k6-wo.name: Where?
werkzeug.k6-wo.regel: Rule: Chapter 6, plan question 1, the table of the five situations from top to bottom. Center closed (both center files locked): play on the wing your chain points to, with the lever against the enemy base. Center open (no locked pawns): play with pieces in the middle. A counterstrike can be an existing tension in the center (counted on the square of the attacked pawn) or a lever by one square or with the double step from the starting position (counted on the target square, as if the pawn were already there). Kings on opposite wings (both castled): for both sides, the app counts the pawn moves up to the first lever against a shield pawn (double step counts as one move, occupied squares block) and names your open and half-open files toward the enemy king. Kings on the same wing: the three conditions as a checklist (center closed or without an enemy lever against your center pawns; more attackers than defenders in the attack sector, as with the golden attack rule; a square in the pawn shield that only the king defends and that one of your pieces attacks, or a hook). No attack in sight: against an enemy pawn that no pawn can defend any more and that is fixed (the square in front of it is occupied or guarded by your pawn), otherwise the minority attack (at least two pawns, a lever, against an enemy majority with a candidate); if your king stands there, counterplay with pieces. The answer is the first situation from the top that names a place. If the side to move is in check or its queen is attacked (by a cheaper piece, or undefended), the app only says: first answer the check (the threat).
werkzeug.k6-wo.erklaerung: Plan question 1: where do I play? The app checks the center, the kings and the weaknesses according to the table in Chapter 6.
werkzeug.k6-wo.legende: Gold: your own pawn storm or lever. Red: the enemy pawn storm. Gray: a target in the enemy pawn shield.
werkzeug.k6-gegner.name: Opponent?
werkzeug.k6-gegner.regel: Rule: Chapter 6, plan question 2. The opponent's plan is his answer to plan question 1: his lever against your chain base, his pawn storm against your pawn shield, or his counterstrike in the center (automatic assessment). Plus what he threatens now (Chess X-ray, question 3) and what you need to secure: the base under his lever, the shield pawn under his storm, squares in front of your king that only the king defends. In the card below, the engine calculates what he would play if he were to move now (null move; not in check). The five means of defense: bring in defenders (pieces that reach the sector around your king in one move), close the line or defend the square, counterstrike in the center (your lever), trade off attackers (his pieces in the sector, above all the queen), give back material (if you are up material). If the side to move is in check or its queen is attacked, the app only says: first answer the check (the threat).
werkzeug.k6-gegner.erklaerung: Plan question 2: what does my opponent want? The app names his plan, his threats and what you need to secure; below, the engine shows what he would play if he were to move now. Plus the five means of defense.
werkzeug.k6-gegner.legende: Red arrows: the opponent's plan (lever, pawn storm) and, below, his best move according to the engine. Gold arrow: your own counterstrike in the center.
werkzeug.k6-lap.name: LAP
werkzeug.k6-lap.regel: Rule: Chapter 6, plan question 3 (LAP principle). For every piece except king and pawns, the app counts the free target squares (squares it can move to; your own pieces block). The least active is: a minor piece still on its starting square; otherwise the minor piece with the fewest squares; rooks and queen come after that (they belong on files, not in the crowd). Suggestion according to Chapter 5 (automatic assessment): a knight to a safe square or knight square it reaches in at most three moves (your own pieces in the way must make room, squares under enemy pawn fire are blocked), otherwise to the square from which it attacks the most squares in the enemy half; rooks to the open, otherwise half-open file, and from there to the 7th rank; if two rooks are doubled on an open file, the front one penetrates to the 7th rank if the square there is safe (this takes priority over the suggestion); bishops to a safe square with more scope, bad bishops into the trade; the queen last. Exchange question: the opponent's most active piece (most squares) and the space rule from Chapter 5. If the side to move is in check or its queen is attacked, the app only says: first answer the check (the threat).
werkzeug.k6-lap.erklaerung: Plan question 3: which piece do I bring there? The app counts the free squares of every piece, names the least active one and suggests a target for it. Plus the exchange question.
werkzeug.k6-lap.legende: Red: the least active piece. Gold: its route to the target. Gray: pieces that make room.
werkzeug.k6-planbilanz.name: Plan balance
werkzeug.k6-planbilanz.regel: Rule: Chapter 6, plan balance. The three plan questions for both sides side by side, with the same rules as the tools Where?, Opponent? and LAP, plus the plan in one sentence (“I use …, attack … and secure …”, automatic assessment). If the book has a plan balance for this figure, it appears below. If the side to move is in check or its queen is attacked, the app only says: first answer the check (the threat); plan questions apply in quiet positions.
werkzeug.k6-planbilanz.erklaerung: The plan balance answers the three plan questions for both sides and sums up each plan in one sentence.
werkzeug.k6-planbilanz.legende: For the side in view, as with Where? and LAP: gold your own pawn storm or lever and the route of the least active piece, red the enemy pawn storm and that piece, gray targets in the pawn shield and pieces that make room.

werkzeug.k7-warnsignale.name: W1–W7
werkzeug.k7-warnsignale.regel: Rule: Chapter 7, step 1. W1 to W5 as in Chapter 4 (see Warning signs). W6 Fork geometry: a square that a knight or pawn reaches in one move and from which it attacks two enemy targets: the king, a more valuable piece or an undefended piece, including an undefended pawn (defended pawns don't count). That is how the fork wins material, because the opponent can save only one of the targets. The fork square is gray; if the fork threatens you, its targets are red. W7 Piece on the edge (automatic assessment): knight, bishop, rook or queen with at most two safe squares, if the piece is attacked, stands on the edge of the board or in the enemy half. For every sign that lights up, the motifs from the book's table “From warning sign to motif”, plus “Passed pawn on the second-to-last rank” and “You are losing” (at least one minor piece down).
werkzeug.k7-warnsignale.erklaerung: Tactics, step 1: where is it worth looking? All seven warning signs of both sides with labels on the board, and for each sign the motifs to look for.
werkzeug.k7-warnsignale.legende: Red with label: warning signs for the side in view. Gold: signs for the opponent. Gray with W6: fork squares, plus red for the targets of an enemy fork.
werkzeug.k7-erzwingend.name: Forcing moves
werkzeug.k7-erzwingend.regel: Rule: Chapter 7, step 2. The forcing moves of your side in calculation order: first all checks, then all captures (with the balance of the exchange calculation, best first), then moves that set up a new threat (mate or winning material on the next move). A check that also captures is listed only with the checks. Numbers on the board in this order, at most twelve. Then the engine calculates the first six candidates one after another until things are quiet, as with the Quiet tool (until each side makes one move without a check and without a capture), and adds the balance: material at the end minus material before, from your point of view, with the most important piece you win or lose, and the engine's value (from White's point of view). The strongest candidate is the one with the engine's best value, a mate counts most; it gets a “!” on the board. The other candidates that win no material and give no mate by the time things are quiet turn gray. If it is not your move, the app calculates as if the opponent had passed. If you are in check, the defense questions come first.
werkzeug.k7-erzwingend.erklaerung: Tactics, step 2: what do you calculate first? All candidates with numbers on the board: checks, then captures, then threats. Calculate them in this order, each branch until things are quiet; the engine calculates the first six for you and shows the balance.

werkzeug.k7-motiv.name: Motif
werkzeug.k7-motiv.regel: Rule: Chapter 7, the twelve basic motifs and the mating patterns. The app replays the solution (the next move in the book with its continuation, otherwise the last move) and checks the key move. If the side to move is in check, the sequence that led to it counts: all checks up to the figure, and with an in-between check after a capture also the move before it. Checked are: double check (two checking pieces), discovered attack (another piece gives check or attacks), fork and double attack (the moved piece attacks two targets: king, more valuable or undefended piece, undefended pawn), skewer and pin (new line), promotion, trapped piece (attacked without a safe square). From the sequence: clearance (the next piece of your own moves to the cleared square), deflection (the piece that took the bait was blocking the line of the follow-up move), decoy (the follow-up move hits the piece on the bait square or gives mate), removing the defender (the key move captures the defender of the follow-up target square), overloading (the target square was held by a piece with two duties, W4), battery (the move drives away the defender of the battery's target square), intermezzo (the key move leaves material hanging, and the capture is followed by a check or capture), desperado (the piece that is lost anyway takes something with check), perpetual check (only checks without captures, by the side that is at least one minor piece behind), stalemate (capturing the bait gives stalemate). If the key move moves a relatively pinned piece, “Relative pin broken” is added. Mating patterns at the end of the sequence or as a threat; Boden's mate only if the two bishops alone control all escape squares. Automatic assessment; for the book's exercises, the book's motif is shown next to it.

werkzeug.k7-ruhe.name: Quiet
werkzeug.k7-ruhe.regel: Rule: Chapter 7, step 3. The engine calculates its main line and cuts it after the last check or capture: that is the quiet point (“until no check, no capture and no threat is in the air any more”); if the line ends in mate or in the middle of captures, the card says so. The moves are shown in steps of at most four half-moves; the balance counts the material from the point of view of the side to move before and at the end, plus the engine's value. Without the engine, the tool names the four checkpoints (strongest reply: the opponent's in-between checks; your own king: his mating threats; move order; balance) and, for the strongest enemy threat, the five defense questions (capture, move away, defend, interpose, counterthreat) with clues from the position. Automatic assessment.

werkzeug.k8-regeln.name: Six rules
werkzeug.k8-regeln.regel: Rule: Chapter 8, the six golden endgame rules. For each rule, the app checks what can be seen of it in the position: rule 1 the king's position and its shortest safe route (gold arrows) to the key squares of your own passed pawn, otherwise to the center; rule 2 the opposition; rule 3 the outside passed pawn as a second weakness, or the pawn race; rule 4 the material balance (more: trade pieces, less: trade pawns); rule 5 passive kings behind the pawns and rooks with few squares; rule 6 every passed pawn with the moves until promotion, the promotion square and the key squares. Approximation: the king's route is calculated with the pieces where they stand.
werkzeug.k8-regeln.erklaerung: Endgame: the six golden rules applied to this position.
werkzeug.k8-opposition.name: Opposition
werkzeug.k8-opposition.regel: Rule: Chapter 8, rule 2 and “Distant and diagonal opposition”. The kings stand in opposition when they are on one file or rank with one square (direct), three or five squares (distant) between them, or on a diagonal with one or three squares between them. The player who is not to move has the opposition. The app only names opposition moves that hold the result: in king and pawn versus king exactly, with an endgame tablebase; in pure pawn endgames with more pawns, only moves that don't give up a pawn. It names the distant opposition with five squares after the one with three squares and adds “whether that is enough is shown by the key squares”. If no opposition move holds the result, it says what decides instead: the stalemate, the square, a pawn move, the spare tempo or another king move. Gray: the squares between the kings. Gold: the squares on which the king to move takes the opposition and holds the result. Gold arrow: the move that decides instead; red arrow: the move that gives stalemate.
werkzeug.k8-opposition.erklaerung: Endgame: are the kings in opposition, who has it, and which moves take it?
werkzeug.k8-opposition.legende: Gray: the squares between the kings. Gold: the squares on which a king takes the opposition and holds the result. Gold arrow: the move that decides instead; red arrow: the stalemating move.
werkzeug.k8-quadrat.name: Square
werkzeug.k8-quadrat.regel: Rule: Chapter 8, “The rule of the square”. From the passed pawn to the promotion square, toward the side of the enemy king, a square is formed. If the enemy king can step into it when it is his move, he catches the pawn. As in the book, the square always starts at the pawn. Side to move: if the pawn's side is to move, the pawn moves first; then the square shrinks by one rank, and the king must be able to step into the smaller square. Double step: if the pawn stands on its starting square, also one rank further. Gold: the pawn's route; gray: the other sides; the enemy king gold if he catches the pawn, red if the pawn runs through. Caveats according to the chess tip: the rule applies to a single passed pawn that its own king does not help and that nothing stops. Therefore the app gives no verdict when your own king stands in front of or next to the pawn (then key squares and opposition count) and when connected passed pawns protect each other; the king is then gray. A pawn behind a pawn of its own on the same file does not count as a passed pawn of your own. If a pawn becomes a passed pawn with the next move, the app checks its square in the position after that move and names it first.
werkzeug.k8-quadrat.erklaerung: Endgame: does the king catch the passed pawn? The square, with side to move and double step. Tap a passed pawn to select it.
werkzeug.k8-quadrat.legende: Gold arrow: the pawn's route. Gray: the other sides of the square. King gold if he reaches the square, red if not, gray if the rule gives no verdict here.
werkzeug.k8-schluesselfelder.name: Key squares
werkzeug.k8-schluesselfelder.regel: Rule: Chapter 8, “Key squares: where the king wants to go”. Pawn on the 2nd, 3rd or 4th rank: the three squares two ranks in front of it; 5th or 6th rank: the six squares one and two ranks in front of it; rook pawn: the last two squares of the neighboring file. If the king of the pawn's side stands on a key square, he wins, no matter who is to move, as long as the pawn is not lost immediately. Gold: the key squares of your own passed pawns and the king move to get there; red: those of the enemy passed pawns (his king must not get there). Special case 6th rank: whether the pawn reaches the 7th rank without check; if it gets there without check and the pawn's side is to move, the conclusion names the pawn move.
werkzeug.k8-schluesselfelder.erklaerung: Endgame: the key squares of both sides' passed pawns and whether the king occupies or reaches them.
werkzeug.k8-schluesselfelder.legende: Gold: key squares of your own passed pawns and the king move to get there. Red: the opponent's key squares.
werkzeug.k8-elementarmatt.name: Basic mates
werkzeug.k8-elementarmatt.regel: Rule: Chapter 8, basic mates with queen, rook or two bishops against the lone king. Gray: the box, that is, the squares the king still has left (via squares the strong side does not attack). Gold: moves that give mate at once. Red: moves that give stalemate. Plus, when the strong side is to move: checks that safely shrink the box (driving moves), quiet moves that shrink it (blocking moves, gray arrows), and moves of the blocking piece that leave the box unchanged and keep it out of the king's reach (waiting moves, rook and queen). Facing each other: the kings on one file or rank with one square between them.
werkzeug.k8-elementarmatt.erklaerung: Endgame: queen, rook or two bishops against the king. The app shows the box, the mating moves and the moves that give stalemate.
werkzeug.k8-elementarmatt.legende: Gray: the box and the blocking moves. Gold arrows: mating moves. Red arrows: moves that give stalemate.

werkzeug.k9-turmbegriffe.name: Rook endgame
werkzeug.k9-turmbegriffe.regel: Rule: Chapter 9, “Three terms for every rook endgame”. The terms apply to rook and one pawn versus rook (and rook versus pawn); if there are several pawns on the board, the tool refers you to the recognition pattern. The attacker is the side with the most advanced passed pawn. Cutting off: the attacker's rook stands on a file (or rank) between the defending king and the pawn; the files in between are counted, and from three on it is often enough to win. Checking distance: the files between the defending rook and the pawn, at least three. Short and long side: the files next to the pawn up to the edge; the defender's king belongs on the short side, the rook on the long side. If the defending king stands in front of the pawn and the attacking king is not yet in front of its pawn, checking distance and sides don't apply: then Philidor applies (rook on the defender's 3rd rank, after the pawn move give checks from behind). Gray: blocking line and checking distance; the defender's king and rook gold if they are placed correctly, otherwise red.
werkzeug.k9-turmbegriffe.erklaerung: Rook endgame with a passed pawn: is the king cut off, does the rook have checking distance, are king and rook on the right side?
werkzeug.k9-turmbegriffe.legende: Gray arrows: blocking line and checking distance. The defender's king and rook gold if they are placed correctly, otherwise red.
werkzeug.k9-erkennungsbilder.name: Recognition pattern
werkzeug.k9-erkennungsbilder.regel: Rule: Chapter 9, review table. The app goes through the recognition questions from top to bottom: rook and pawn versus rook (Lucena: pawn on the 7th rank, king in front of it, enemy king cut off to the side; Vancura: far-advanced rook pawn with the rook in front of it; Philidor: defending king in front of the pawn; otherwise short side), rook versus pawn, rook endgame with several pawns (rook behind the passed pawn), queen versus pawn (bishop pawn or rook pawn, stalemate after the capture), queen versus queen, rook versus bishop (corner), bishop endgames (same or opposite colors, wrong bishop; with opposite-colored bishops the app counts the passed pawns: two that are at least three files apart are called separated and usually win, close or connected ones allow a fortress draw), bishop versus knight (wings), knight. Exact (E) when the book's standard position has been reached, otherwise approximation (N) with the plan from the table.
werkzeug.k9-erkennungsbilder.erklaerung: Endgame deep dive: which pattern from the table is on the board, and which plan follows from it?
werkzeug.k9-erkennungsbilder.legende: The key square of the pattern, such as the passed pawn or a king: gold if it speaks for the plan, red if it endangers it, gray for orientation.
turmbegriffe.titel: Three terms for the rook endgame
turmbegriffe.keinsTitel: No rook endgame with a passed pawn
turmbegriffe.keins: The three terms apply to rook endgames with a passed pawn; here the rook or the passed pawn is missing.
turmbegriffe.abschneiden.ja: The rook {turm} blocks a file between the king {koenig} and the pawn: {dazwischen} in between (gray arrow).
turmbegriffe.abschneiden.nein: The king {koenig} is not cut off: no rook blocks a file or rank between it and the pawn.
turmbegriffe.abschneiden.reicht: Rule of thumb: from three files on, it is often enough to win.
turmbegriffe.abschneiden.wenig: Rule of thumb: the more files in between, the better for the attacker; from three on, it is often enough.
turmbegriffe.schachdistanz.keinTurm: The defender has no rook: no checking distance to measure.
turmbegriffe.schachdistanz.linien: Between the rook {turm} and the pawn {bauer}: {linien} (needed: {soll}).
turmbegriffe.schachdistanz.reicht: That is enough for its checks: if the king walks toward it, the king leaves its pawn.
turmbegriffe.schachdistanz.zuNah: Too close: the king walks toward the rook without leaving its pawn, and the checks stop.
turmbegriffe.seiten.links: Next to the pawn {bauer}: on the left {links} files to the edge (short side), on the right {rechts} (long side).
turmbegriffe.seiten.linksEins: Next to the pawn {bauer}: on the left 1 file to the edge (short side), on the right {rechts} (long side).
turmbegriffe.seiten.rechts: Next to the pawn {bauer}: on the right {rechts} files to the edge (short side), on the left {links} (long side).
turmbegriffe.seiten.rechtsEins: Next to the pawn {bauer}: on the right 1 file to the edge (short side), on the left {links} (long side).
turmbegriffe.seiten.gleich: Next to the pawn {bauer}: both sides are equally long ({links} files).
turmbegriffe.koenigAuf.kurz: The king {koenig} is on the short side (correct).
turmbegriffe.koenigAuf.lang: The king {koenig} is on the long side: it belongs on the short one.
turmbegriffe.koenigAuf.gleich: The king {koenig} stands next to the pawn; both sides are equally long.
turmbegriffe.koenigAuf.bauernlinie: The king {koenig} is on the pawn's file (in front of it: Philidor).
turmbegriffe.turmAuf.kurz: The rook {turm} is on the short side: it belongs on the long one, with checking distance.
turmbegriffe.turmAuf.lang: The rook {turm} is on the long side (correct).
turmbegriffe.turmAuf.gleich: The rook {turm} stands next to the pawn; both sides are equally long.
turmbegriffe.turmAuf.bauernlinie: The rook {turm} is on the pawn's file (behind or in front of it).
turmbegriffe.fazit: {angreifer} attacks with the pawn {bauer}; the defending king is {abgeschnitten}.
bilder.titel: Recognition patterns of the endgame deep dive
bilder.keins: No pattern from the table fits: the recognition questions apply to rook, queen, bishop and knight endgames with little material.
bilder.verweis: More on this in the book: Chapter 9, “Review: the recognition patterns”.
bilder.fazitStandard: {name}: the book's standard position is on the board.
bilder.fazitBild: {name}: the pattern, but not yet the standard position.
bilder.philidor.name: Philidor position
bilder.philidor.frage: The defending king stands in front of the pawn.
bilder.philidor.plan: The rook blocks the rank directly in front of the pawn so that the attacking king cannot come forward. If the pawn steps onto that rank, the rook switches behind and gives check after check.
bilder.philidor.sperren: The rook blocks rank {reihe} from the side, far from the enemy king
bilder.philidor.hinten: The pawn is on rank {reihe}: the rook switches behind and gives checks
bilder.kurzeSeite.name: King to the short side
bilder.kurzeSeite.frage: The defending king has been pushed away from the promotion square.
bilder.kurzeSeite.plan: The king goes to the side of the pawn with fewer files, the rook to the other. At least three files between rook and pawn, so that the checks from the side work.
bilder.kurzeSeite.turm: Rook on the long side with checking distance {linien} (needed: {soll})
bilder.lucena.name: Lucena position
bilder.lucena.frage: The pawn is on the seventh rank, its king in front of it, the other king cut off to the side.
bilder.lucena.plan: Building a bridge: first push the other king one more file away with a rook check, then put the rook on the fourth rank. The king leaves the promotion square in a zigzag; when checks come from the side, the rook steps in between, defended.
bilder.lucena.lage: The enemy king stands {linien} beside the pawn, cut off by the rook
bilder.vancura.name: Vancura position
bilder.vancura.frage: A far-advanced rook pawn, with the attacker's rook in front of it.
bilder.vancura.plan: The defender's rook attacks the pawn from the side and gives check from there. The king waits on g7 or h7 (with the h-pawn on a7 or b7).
bilder.vancura.turm: The defending rook attacks the pawn from the side
bilder.turmGegenBauer.name: Rook against pawn
bilder.turmGegenBauer.frage: Is the king of the pawn's side cut off, and which king arrives in time?
bilder.turmGegenBauer.plan: Cut the king off with the rook and count the moves to promotion. The defender keeps underpromotion in mind. Two connected pawns on the sixth rank are stronger than the rook.
bilder.turmGegenBauer.abgeschnitten: The king of the pawn's side is cut off ({dazwischen} in between)
bilder.turmGegenBauer.frei: The king of the pawn's side is not cut off
bilder.turmGegenBauer.rennen: Race: the pawn needs {schritte}, its king is {angreifer} from the pawn, the rook's king {verteidiger} from the promotion square
bilder.mehrbauern.name: Rook endgame with several pawns
bilder.mehrbauern.frage: How active is the rook, and is it behind a passed pawn?
bilder.mehrbauern.plan: Make the rook active, attack a second weakness, then trade into a won pawn endgame. An extra pawn on just one wing, say four against three, often does not win.
bilder.mehrbauern.hinterEigen: The rook {turm} is behind its own passed pawn {bauer} (gold)
bilder.mehrbauern.hinterFremd: The rook {turm} is behind the enemy passed pawn {bauer} (red)
bilder.mehrbauern.keiner: No rook is behind a passed pawn
bilder.dameGegenBauer.name: Queen against pawn
bilder.dameGegenBauer.frage: Is it a bishop pawn or a rook pawn, and would the capture be stalemate?
bilder.dameGegenBauer.plan: The queen forces the king in front of its pawn with checks. In every pause your own king moves one step closer, until the pawn falls with check.
bilder.dameGegenBauer.laeufer: Bishop pawn {bauer}: stalemate alert, often a draw (Fig. 9.31)
bilder.dameGegenBauer.rand: Rook pawn {bauer}: stalemate alert, often a draw
bilder.dameGegenBauer.mitte: Pawn {bauer} on the b-, d-, e- or g-file: the queen wins
bilder.dameGegenBauer.schlagGeht: Capturing on {bauer} does not give stalemate
bilder.dameGegenDame.name: Queen against queen
bilder.dameGegenDame.frage: Can the defender give perpetual check?
bilder.dameGegenDame.plan: The defender calculates every check. The attacker first brings his king into shelter.
bilder.laeufer.name: Bishop endgame
bilder.laeufer.frage: Same-colored or opposite-colored bishops? A wrong bishop? Can the passed pawns be blockaded?
bilder.laeufer.plan: The defender builds a fortress: he blockades on the squares of the color that the enemy bishop never reaches.
bilder.laeufer.gleich: Same-colored bishops: the passed pawn decides
bilder.laeufer.ungleichGetrennt: Opposite-colored bishops, separated passed pawns {bauer} and {partner}: usually won, because king and bishop cannot blockade on both wings at once
bilder.laeufer.zaehlen: Rule of the book: count the passed pawns that cannot be blockaded
bilder.laeufer.falsch: Wrong bishop: the bishop does not control the promotion square {ecke}, and the king is in the corner: draw
bilder.laeufer.falschFern: Wrong bishop: the bishop does not control the promotion square {ecke}; a draw if the king reaches the corner
bilder.springer.name: Knight endgame
bilder.springer.frage: Can the passed pawns be blockaded?
bilder.springer.plan: The knight does not work from a distance: count the moves it needs to reach the decisive square.
bilder.springer.tempi: Knight: count the tempi to the promotion square
bilder.laeuferGegenSpringer.name: Bishop against knight
bilder.laeuferGegenSpringer.frage: Are there pawns on both wings or only on one?
bilder.laeuferGegenSpringer.plan: With pawns on both wings the bishop is stronger, because it switches sides quickly. On one wing the knight is often better.
bilder.laeuferGegenSpringer.beide: Pawns on both wings: advantage bishop
bilder.laeuferGegenSpringer.einer: Pawns on only one wing: often advantage knight
bilder.turmGegenLaeufer.name: Rook against bishop
bilder.turmGegenLaeufer.frage: In which corner is the king of the bishop's side?
bilder.turmGegenLaeufer.plan: The bishop's side flees into the corner whose color the bishop does not have.
bilder.turmGegenLaeufer.richtig: The corner {ecke} is the opposite color to the bishop: the right corner
bilder.turmGegenLaeufer.falsch: The corner {ecke} is the bishop's color: the wrong corner
turmbegriffe.abschneiden.reihe: The rook {turm} blocks rank {reihe}: the king {koenig} can no longer reach the pawn (gray arrow).
turmbegriffe.seiten.rand: Rook pawn {bauer}: there is only one side next to it; the defending king waits on g7/h7 (with the h-pawn a7/b7), see Vancura.
turmbegriffe.seiten.nurEinTurm: Short and long side apply to rook and pawn against rook; here only one side has a rook.
turmbegriffe.philidor.distanz: The king {koenig} stands in front of the pawn: checking distance does not apply here.
turmbegriffe.philidor.seiten: Short and long side only apply once Philidor no longer works: the king {koenig} stands in front of the pawn.
turmbegriffe.philidor.plan: Philidor: rook on your 3rd rank; after the pawn advances, give checks from behind.
turmbegriffe.mehrbauern: The three terms and the reference to Vancura apply to rook and one pawn against rook; here there are several pawns on the board.
turmbegriffe.mehrbauernBild: Take a look at the recognition pattern “{name}”.
bilder.turmGegenBauer.zweiVerbundene: Two connected pawns on the 6th rank: they beat the rook (Fig. 9.22)
werkzeug.k11-phase.name: Phase
werkzeug.k11-phase.regel: Rule: Chapter 12, thinking routine step 1, and Chapter 8, “When does the endgame begin”. Endgame if the four check questions mostly (at least three) come out yes: queens off the board; both kings safe from a mating attack (without queens and without a mate threat in one move); your own king can reach the center via unattacked squares; the pawns decide. Opening as long as the opening goals have not been met; the app reads this as development: middlegame as soon as one side is developed (at most one minor piece on its starting square, as in the book at Fig. 12.1) or the piece material is unequal by at least one minor piece; opening as long as both sides still have two or more minor pieces at home. A king that has not castled is a question of king safety, not of the phase. The pawns decide: a passed pawn, or a pawn majority with little piece material (at most 13 points per side without pawns). One extra rule that does not come from the book and is labeled as such in the display: endgame as soon as each side has at most 13 points in pieces and pawns besides the king (Speelman), even with queens on the board. The phase is the same for both sides; the question about the king in the center is asked for the side to move. For each phase, the tools from the summary page; for the example games from Chapter 11, the row of the book's table. Approximation. Gold: in the endgame, the route of the king of the side to move into the center.
werkzeug.k11-phase.erklaerung: Which phase, which tool? Opening goals and the four endgame questions, plus, for example games, the book's theme, tool and lesson.
werkzeug.k11-phase.legende: Gold arrows in the endgame: the route of the king of the side to move into the center.
werkzeug.k12-erfassen.name: Assess
werkzeug.k12-erfassen.regel: Rule: Chapter 12, thinking routine step 1. The opponent's last move (from the game history) and his threats on the next move (winning material, mate), red arrows; the warning signs W1 to W7 on both sides with their markings (Chapters 4 and 7); the phase with opening goals and endgame questions, and the tools for step 2.
werkzeug.k12-erfassen.erklaerung: Thinking routine, step 1: what did the last move change, what is threatened? Warning signs of both sides, phase and tool.
werkzeug.k12-erfassen.legende: Red arrows: the opponent's threats. Plus the warning signs as with W1–W7: red for the side in view, gold for the opponent, gray fork squares.
werkzeug.k12-kandidaten.name: Candidates
werkzeug.k12-kandidaten.regel: Rule: Chapter 12, thinking routine steps 2 to 4. Step 2: candidates in calculation order (at most two each of checks, captures without loss, moves with a new threat), plus the next book move as a quiet candidate; if the opponent threatens mate in one, a move that parries it (defense against a threat, preferably without losing a piece and while developing a minor piece); if nothing is forcing, the card names the tool for the phase. In check, all defensive moves are the candidates (move the king, capture the attacker, interpose; glossary “Check”), the book move first. Step 3: for each candidate, the opponent's strongest reply in the order mate, winning capture, check, threat, red for the first candidate; if the replying piece then attacks two targets, it is called a fork (Chapter 7, W6). Step 4: material balance after candidate and reply; then the best candidate. If a candidate is answered with mate, it is ruled out regardless of material; if it gives mate itself, it is the best. If your own king then stands in the open (see Safety check), the card says so too. Approximation, one move deep; the calculation until things are quiet is done by the Quiet tool (Chapter 7).
werkzeug.k12-kandidaten.erklaerung: Thinking routine, steps 2 to 4: collect candidates, the strongest reply to each candidate, the balance afterwards.
werkzeug.k12-kandidaten.legende: Gold arrows: the candidates, in check all defensive moves. Red arrow: the strongest reply to the first one.
werkzeug.k12-sicherheitsblick.name: Safety check
werkzeug.k12-sicherheitsblick.regel: Rule: Chapter 12, safety check before moving, three questions about the move being checked (the next book move or a move of your own via Move): is my king safe afterwards (mate in one, king in the open, free neighboring squares, the opponent's checks)? Can the opponent capture the moved piece at once (exchange balance)? Do I allow a check or even a mate? King in the open: it has left its back rank, stands without a pawn shield (fewer than two of its own pawns directly in front of it or one square further) and the opponent attacks at least two neighboring squares; this only applies as long as the opponent has a queen (in the endgame the king belongs in the center, Chapter 8). Example Fig. 12.3: 3... f5. Gold: the move; red: the capture of the piece, the checks allowed and the attacked neighboring squares.
werkzeug.k12-sicherheitsblick.erklaerung: Before moving: is the king safe, can the opponent capture the moved piece, do I allow a check or mate? Applies to the next book move or a move of your own.
werkzeug.k12-sicherheitsblick.legende: Gold arrow: the move being checked. Red arrows: captures and checks it allows the opponent. Red squares: attacked neighboring squares of the king in the open.

phase.ist.zuHause: Opening: both sides still have two or more minor pieces on their starting squares, and the piece material is equal.
phase.ist.beideEntwickelt: Middlegame: both sides are developed (at most one minor piece still on its starting square); the endgame questions do not yet mostly answer yes.
phase.ist.eineEntwickelt: Middlegame: {farbe} is developed (at most one minor piece still on its starting square); the other side's lag in development is a middlegame theme. The endgame questions do not yet mostly answer yes.
phase.ist.materialUngleich: Middlegame: the piece material differs by at least one minor piece, so the opening is over, even if minor pieces are still on their starting squares.
phase.ist.glossarMittelspiel: Middlegame: both sides are developed (at most one minor piece still on its starting square) and have castled, as the glossary requires; the endgame questions do not yet mostly answer yes.
phase.ist.glossarEroeffnung: Opening: according to the glossary, the middlegame only begins once both sides are developed and have castled. Still open: {offen}.
phase.ist.fragen: Endgame: the four check questions mostly answer yes.
phase.ist.wenigMaterial: Endgame: little material (extra rule, see below).
phase.zusatz.wenigMaterial: Extra rule (not from the book): each side has at most {punkte} points of material besides the king (pawn 1, bishop and knight 3, rook 5, queen 9). Such positions are generally regarded as endgames (Speelman), even with queens on the board. By the book's four questions, the phase would be: {buch}.

botstaerke.erklaerung: The number comes from many games of the bots against each other and against the plain levels (an Elo ladder built from the results). Its position is anchored to the scale of “Your playing strength”, the average of chess.com and Lichess: someone who plays ten games the way this bot does would see roughly this number there. It is accurate to about ±150 and applies to the whole game, not to each phase. Above 2200, “Your playing strength” has no calibration data anymore; there the number comes only from the results against the weaker levels and is less accurate (about ±200). Below 400 only the limit is shown. Without extra mistakes the ten levels are calibrated to 300 Elo per level; level 1 plays almost randomly and is already at the limit. Custom levels and custom bots have never been measured; their number is estimated from the three levels per phase, minus what the ticked extra mistakes and blind spots cost on average (measured per level), and is less accurate, because style is not taken into account. A ready-made bot is listed under the level of its measured number (300 per level); the heading of each level shows the range of its bots, and the ranges of neighboring levels do not overlap. Rated games use the bot's number as the opponent's rating.

spielen.eigene.fehlerartenHinweis: The ticks decide which extra mistakes it makes; how often follows humans of its strength (rated Lichess games). Extra mistakes make it more human and somewhat weaker than its levels. Without ticks it plays exactly its levels.
spielen.stilHinweis: Aggressive: among equally good moves, the opponent prefers moves into your half of the board, into the quarter around your king, captures and checks. Defensive: moves into its own half, toward its own king, no captures. The style chooses among moves that are up to 0.3 pawns per style step away from the move of the set level, both up and down; so on average the playing strength stays about the same. Only on level 10, where the level's move is already the best one, does a style make it weaker, “very aggressive” or “very defensive” by about one level.
spielen.eigene.blindeFleckenHinweis: Kinds of move it overlooks like humans of its strength; in the advanced mode also less often or up to three times as often. It always sees the ones without a tick. The review names it, e.g. “missed a retreat”.
spielen.eigene.erweitertHinweis: 100 % means as often as humans of its strength, 0 % never, 300 % three times as often. The overall frequency applies to all extra mistakes and blind spots together; the levels set the base strength. The maximum loss limits how costly a mistake of this kind may be (in pawns); without a limit the bot chooses like humans, cheap mistakes more often than costly ones. The displayed strength is an estimate.

rueckblick.balkenInfo: The bar to the left of the board shows who stands better: the further the light part reaches, the better White stands; in the middle the position is equal. The number is the engine's evaluation (Stockfish 19) from White's point of view, roughly in pawns: +1 means about a pawn better, −2 two pawns worse, “M3” mate in three moves. Stockfish derives this number from the winning chance; a whole extra piece in the opening therefore often gives 5 to 7 instead of 3 as in the book's table of values, and chess.com usually shows smaller numbers. That is why the card for a mistake gives the winning chance before and after, and the explanation gives the material by the book's values.
spielstaerke.erklaerung: Accuracy: 100% means every move was the best; one serious mistake counts for more than many good moves. You choose how it is calculated at the top of this card (like Lichess, app or chess.com). The estimated playing strength is a rough number derived from accuracy, from ten moves before the decision on, calibrated on 300 rated rapid games each from chess.com and Lichess; it does not depend on the switch. A single game is often 400 points off, which is why a range is shown; over ten games it gets narrower (card “Your playing strength” under Play). The engine on a low level makes deliberate mistakes and gets correspondingly low numbers. For playing strength and the word for each phase, only the moves until the game is decided count: until one side has at least 90% winning chance and keeps it to the end. After that almost every move is “accurate” because there is nothing left to lose; otherwise a game thrown away early would get a high number. The accuracy at the top counts all moves, as Lichess and chess.com do. The word for each phase sums up the accuracy as Lichess does (outstanding from 95%, very good from 88%, good from 78%, inaccurate from 68%, flawed from 55%). Tactics are the moves from positions with a check, a threat or a winning capture (Safety check, Chapter 12); strategy, the moves from quiet positions. For each phase, the verdict and accuracy are always shown; the playing-strength number only from six moves in the phase, because below that it varies too much. By the book's rules the opening often ends earlier.

startseite.untertitel: A handbook for beginners and improving players
startseite.meta: Schach von Grund auf: the handbook for beginners and advancing players, with the app for the book. Every figure as a live board, the book's tools, training and an engine.
startseite.buch.text1: From the first move to the ideas that matter on the way toward 2000 Elo: the book leads from the rules and chess notation through the principles of the opening, gambits and traps, pawn structures, finding a plan and tactics, all the way to the important endgames.
startseite.buch.text2: Each chapter gives you a tool to check positions yourself. At the end, studies, annotated games and a training section bring everything together into a thinking routine for your own games.

einstellungen.wischen.hinweis: Tapping the piece and the target square always works. A swipe only starts on a piece that is allowed to move; on all other squares the page scrolls. Applies on this device as soon as a board is opened anew.
uebung.auftragZug: The task is in the book. Play your side's move on the board; the app replies with the other side's moves from the solution. Diagram in the book:
uebung.auftragDenken: You solve this exercise in your head or on paper. The task is in the book; afterwards you read the explanation here and rate yourself. Diagram in the book:
uebung.erstDenken: Think first: hints and solution appear once you have thought it over.
uebung.erstZug: Think first (strict): hints and solution appear after your first move of your own.
selbstdenken.frage: How do things stand? Take a calm look at the position before the tools and the engine help.
selbstdenken.engineFehler: The engine could not check it right now; compare with the tools yourself.
selbstdenken.stimmt: The engine says: {worte} ({zahl}). Assessed correctly! Next time the tools and the engine are available here right away.
selbstdenken.stimmtNicht: The engine says: {worte} ({zahl}), so “{engine}”. The tools show you why.
selbstdenken.grenze: The engine counts anything up to ±0.5 pawns as equal.
uebung.hinweisZug: The golden arrow shows the move.
uebung.geloest: Correct! That is the book's solution.
uebung.geloestAnders: Correct! This move is just as good. The explanation shows the book's way.
uebung.gezeigt: The book's solution is on the board. The exercise will come up for review soon.
uebung.falsch: That is not the book's move. Try again.
uebung.weiter: Correct. The other side has replied; it is your move again.
uebung.ohneErklaerung: The explanation for this exercise is still to come.
uebung.einzigerZug: Only this move reaches the goal: according to the engine, every other first move is at least one pawn worse.
uebung.eingeschaetzt: Saved. The exercise will come back for review.

dreissig.analyseHinweis: Go through the game more thoroughly. In the review, enter the most important mistake with “Add to mistake log”.
dreissig.keinePartie: No finished game saved yet. Play a game first.
dreissig.bereichHinweis: The four areas take turns. Set yourself just one mini-goal, for example two opposition positions or five exercises with the same motif.

sicherung.erklaerung: A backup is a file with everything the app knows about you: progress, checkmarks, games, rating and settings. Keep it in a safe place. Restoring replaces all data on this device (the app asks first). This is how your data moves to a new device, and how, on the iPhone, it gets from the Safari tab into the installed app. If downloading does not work, use “Share backup” (on phones): with it you can email the file to yourself or save it in Files.
